title.narrative: Enhancing production and consumption of orange fleshed sweet potato by adopting a system strengthening approach

description.narrative: Although Liberia has fertile land and a favorable climate for agriculture, many people in Liberia continue to suffer from food insecurity and malnutrition because the country's food and agricultural systems are inefficient. Chronic food insecurity is on the rise in Liberia due to poverty, gender inequalities, land constraints, unsustainable living conditions and low agricultural production and productivity. One in three children under the age of 5 in Liberia are stunted or too short for their age, because of not getting nutritious food over a long period of time, and frequent bouts of illness. The project aims to adopt a food system approach with emphasis on institutional strengthening to promote the cultivation of orange fleshed sweet potato.

Overall objective: The socio-economic situation and nutritional status of smallholder families in rural areas of Montserrado, Bong, Margibi and Grand Bassa regions, Liberia, are improved.Outcome: 6,200 farmers in the rural areas of Montserrado, Bong, Margibi and Grand Bassa regions use sustainable methods to grow orange-fleshed sweet potatoes and vegetables and have diversified their diets and improved their incomes.

• 4,500 community-based farmers who will benefit from capacity development and inputs to support OFSP cultivation. 180 groups of 25 people each [4,500 people] will benefit from training on savings and credit groups (VSLA) and related equipment kits. • Another 1,700 women farmers receive training and tools for vegetable cultivation. 70% of the targeted project participants are women.• 15 SHED staff members benefiting from capacity building measures• Advisors of the CARI Institute of the Ministry of Agriculture
